rule: GOAL: Move the purple marker up the diagonal dot-line to the blue blob at the top. CONTROLS: Click any gray dot within three steps of the purple to teleport it there. RULE: The purple jumps to the clicked dot; dots below it shift down to fill the gap. TRAP: You cannot click a dot four steps away; that click is a no-op and wastes a move.

GOAL: Move the blue token from the top-left node to the bottom-right node of the 3x3 grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the token two cells in the chosen direction, landing on the next available node. RULE: The token slides to the next open node, leaving a white trail behind it; black cells block movement. TRAP: Assuming the token slides until it hits a wall; it actually moves exactly one lattice step per input.

GOAL: Reach two crosses by growing bars in different directions. CONTROLS: Click glyphs to extend or retract the bar tip. RULE: The bar tip moves opposite to the glyph's gap opening. TRAP: Assuming the gap direction indicated the growth direction, causing initial clicks to shrink the bar instead.

GOAL: Move the yellow key block into the same column as the yellow door by shrinking the lower white area. CONTROLS: The bottom blue button moves the key left by four columns; the top blue button moves it right. RULE: The left edge of the upper white area plus the left edge of the lower white area always equals 84. TRAP: Believing the key must reach the door's row; alignment only requires matching columns, not vertical position.

GOAL: Slide the player's green block right to line up exactly with the door's yellow block at column 27. CONTROLS: Bar 1's bottom button shrank the upper white and grew the middle. Bar 2's bottom button shrank the middle and grew the lower white, moving the player right. RULE: Each press shifted four cells. Alternating the two bars kept the middle stable while the player marched right. TRAP: Assuming the upper white's left edge had to match the door. It didn't; only the player's green needed to overlap.

GOAL: Turn the pink strip so each glyph is the partner of the matching blue glyph. CONTROLS: UP arrow rotates the selected slot's glyph 90 degrees clockwise. RULE: The dictionary pairs each S glyph with one P glyph; match by index, not by shape. TRAP: Thinking the pink glyph must look like the blue glyph; they are different shapes, so match by dictionary position instead.

GOAL: Merge two same-color squares into one bigger square of the next color. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell moves the nearest square of that color to the clicked location. RULE: When two same-color squares are adjacent, clicking between them merges them into a larger square of the next color, centered at the click. TRAP: Squares do not merge just by being close; they must be adjacent or the click must land between them.

GOAL: Reach the red token at the top-right corner. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one cell in the pressed direction. RULE: The red spike only kills if you enter the cell it directly faces; entering from behind or below is safe. TRAP: Thinking the red blocks all adjacent cells or that entering its cell is always fatal.

GOAL: Merge three purple squares into one yellow, then deliver yellow and remaining purple to the two dots. CONTROLS: Click near a square to move it one step toward the click. RULE: A click close to two squares merges them into the next color up. TRAP: Merging requires the click to be within reach of both squares at once, so you must move them close together first.

GOAL: The yellow strip had to match the pink strip slot by slot. CONTROLS: Up arrows cycled the selected slot through its family; Left/Right moved the cursor. RULE: A slot was correct when the yellow glyph matched the pink glyph up to rotation. TRAP: Assuming the current cycle position was the start; the probe had already moved slot 0 six steps, so the search had to begin from the actual state.

ESTABLISHED: The corridor is a horizontal band that extends right and retracts left. Squares inside the band move with it; squares outside stay put. The corridor does not push squares when extending, but retraction forces squares to shift left to remain within the band. FAILED: Extending the corridor right did not move the squares. Clicking (MOUSE) on squares had no effect. UP was blocked. GOAL IS NOT: Aligning the corridor with the R square's row, since the R square is fixed above the player's range. CONTROLS: LEFT retracts the corridor leftward, pushing squares within the band. RIGHT extends

GOAL: align three players with three doors at different rows. CONTROLS: bar buttons shift white space left or right between adjacent columns. RULE: each press moves two units of white space; players stay fixed as columns change width. TRAP: assuming one alignment wins; all three doors must be matched simultaneously.

ESTABLISHED: The tube spans the middle rows; the player is a four-wide block with a cap on one end; two static frames sit at the upper right and lower left. The player can move left and right inside the tube, and the frame follows the player's cap position. FAILED: Moving the player to the upper right area, into the tube's right end, or near the static frames did not clear the level. Pressing SPACE to change the frame's color and then moving did not work. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the upper right corner, touching a static frame, or changing the frame's color. CONTROLS: LEFT and RIGHT move t

ESTABLISHED: The blue bar moves in 4-unit steps, and the win condition appears to be alignment-based rather than requiring the ball to be pushed into a specific spot. FAILED: Moving the blue bar to various positions without aligning it specifically to the ball's edge and the yellow notch's center did not trigger a win. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving the ball or pushing it against the walls; the win requires precise positional alignment of the blue bar. CONTROLS: Left and right arrow keys move the blue bar horizontally by 4 units; the spacebar confirms the position and checks for the win condition.

ESTABLISHED: Panel starts with white cells at the plus positions and gray elsewhere; clicking toggles cells to green or back. A green-at-plus configuration triggered a purple flash, marking a match with the reference card. FAILED: Green-at-plus pattern did not clear the level. Initial all-gray panel did not clear the level. Marker at left or right ends with all-gray panel did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Matching the reference card's plus pattern, nor simply clearing all white cells, nor moving the marker to either extreme end. CONTROLS: Left/Right moves the marker along the track. Clicki

ESTABLISHED: Two yellow pieces on the board: a wide cap at the top-middle and a U-shape at the bottom-middle. The cap spans the middle column; the U spans the middle three columns. FAILED: Various segment mappings where the cap and U were assigned to horizontal or vertical marker rows, including 'wwBww' and 'wBBBw' combinations. GOAL IS NOT: A simple 7-segment digit match using standard top, bottom, left, right, middle segment assignments. CONTROLS: Markers toggle horizontal and vertical bar states. The cap and U pieces indicate specific column groups to be marked.

GOAL: Match the yellow strip's glyph sequence to a target pattern by selecting the correct pair keys. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the selection cursor to choose which pair key to activate. RULE: Each pair key defined a specific sequence of yellow glyphs that had to match the strip exactly. TRAP: Assuming glyphs matched by exact shape rather than rotation, causing false positives and wasted moves.

GOAL: Fill the four panel slots to match the colored order shown at the top. CONTROLS: Click a bottom square to select it (white ring appears), then click a panel slot to swap them. RULE: Matching the reference sequence blue, green, yellow, purple from left to right completes the level. TRAP: Thinking clicking a slot alone places a piece; you must select a source square first, or the swap does nothing useful.

GOAL: Align the yellow strip to the chain translation of the silver strip. CONTROLS: Arrows rotated the strips; each press shifted one position. RULE: Follow the path: Silver maps to Purple, then Purple maps to Yellow. TRAP: Assuming Yellow directly mapped to Silver; the intermediate Purple step was required.

GOAL: Drop the blue bar onto the yellow bar at the ball's column. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the blue bar up/down/left/right; space dropped it. RULE: The bar had to land on the yellow at the same column as the ball. TRAP: Thinking the bar needed to align with the ball's edge or top row; it only needed to cover the yellow's column.

GOAL: Place two crosses so each cross's arms pass through its matching colored markers, clearing all markers. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active cross (up/down/left/right). Space switches the active cross (the white ball moves to the other cross's center). RULE: A cross is defined by its horizontal and vertical arms. Markers are cleared when a cross's arm passes directly through them. TRAP: Believing the ball's position dictates the active cross; in reality, the ball moves to the new active cross's center upon switching, not vice versa.

GOAL: Align the ring of 20 cells so the yellow marker sits on the correct cell. CONTROLS: Click the red arrow to rotate the ring left; click the green arrow to rotate it right. RULE: The yellow dots mark the target position; the ring must be turned until the marker lands there. TRAP: Assuming the arrows moved the marker instead of the entire ring sequence.

GOAL: Guide the two-color piston into the black exit box at the top of the maze. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the 5x5 block; the yellow bar shrank with each move as a timer. RULE: The block could only occupy gray floor tiles; black walls and charcoal holes blocked movement. TRAP: Covering the white plus marker was a decoy; it did not trigger a win and reappeared when uncovered.

GOAL: Align the white diamond with the ring center using the purple midpoint marker. CONTROLS: Click a black cell to move the white diamond; the purple square tracks the line's midpoint. RULE: The white diamond must land exactly on the ring center. TRAP: Believing the gray corner regions were valid targets or that the line needed to be vertical.

ESTABLISHED: The cross occupies rows 30–32, columns 51–53. The green snake's head is vertical. The dot's column is fixed to 40 or 58, never 52. FAILED: All attempts to align the dot with the cross's column and row have failed. The green snake cannot occupy the cross's column without colliding with the vertical bar or the horizontal bar. GOAL IS NOT: Matching the dot to the cross is impossible; the cross is a decoy or a different type of target. CONTROLS: Moving the yellow bar shifts the green snake's body and cap position. The dot follows the green snake's tip.

GOAL: Place the named card's piece into its target slot; the flash shows current and target. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, click a slot to move it, press space to check. RULE: The flash displays the piece's current slot first, then its required slot. TRAP: Assuming the flash indicated which slots to swap rather than where the piece currently is versus where it must go.

GOAL: Move each colored shape so its arms cover all matching markers. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the current shape; space cycled control to the next shape. RULE: A marker was cleared when the shape's edge passed through its cell, regardless of color. TRAP: Believing different colors required different shapes or that the ball indicated the active piece.

GOAL: Slide the two black blocks so they sit directly above the yellow notch. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved both blocks simultaneously in opposite horizontal directions. RULE: The blocks acted as mirror images across the central axis, maintaining a constant combined position. TRAP: Assuming you could move a single block independently to cover the notch, which was impossible under the mirror constraint.

GOAL: Place seven colored tiles into seven slots so each tile lands on the slot named by the flashing pair. CONTROLS: Click a tile in a slot, then click a target slot to swap them. Press space to check. RULE: Each flash showed the tile's current slot first, then its correct slot. TRAP: Assuming the red panel's slots were read in order; the pipe split them, placing red slot 4 last in the sequence.

GOAL: Fill two frames by sliding corridor pieces into their holes. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, then use arrows to slide it one grid step. RULE: A piece fits only when it exactly covers the light gray hole inside a frame. TRAP: You cannot slide a piece into empty background space; moves are blocked unless the destination cells are open or part of the frame.

GOAL: Place seven colored cards into the three panels so the left-to-right reading order matches the reference row. CONTROLS: Click a card in the tray, then click a slot to place it; spacebar checks the answer. RULE: The red panel's open slots are read in sequence, with the green and blue panels' slots inserted between them at the pipe junctions. TRAP: Assuming all slots read strictly left-to-right across the whole board; the pipes dictate that the green and blue panels are read as sub-sequences within the red panel's flow.

GOAL: Turn all eight cells of the highlighted panel red. CONTROLS: Click any cell in the highlighted panel to toggle it blue to red or red to blue. RULE: Each click flips exactly one cell; the highlighted panel is the only one that responds. TRAP: Clicking cells in the non-highlighted panels does nothing, even if they are blue.

GOAL: Light the 7 cells the two glyph stamps mark white, using 6 clicks. CONTROLS: Click a panel cell to toggle blue to orange. RULE: Each glyph is a 3x3 stamp centered on its cell; white cells in the stamp demand orange on the panel. TRAP: Assuming the glyph center cell itself needed coloring; it is not part of the target pattern.

GOAL: Fill the red panel's five slots with the right colors, using a ring to splice in the green panel's two slots. CONTROLS: Click a piece to pick it up, click a slot to drop it; space checks the answer. RULE: The ring must sit in the red slot that lines up with the green panel's connection, so reading left-to-right flows through the green slots. TRAP: Placing the ring by color alone; alignment with the green panel's slot, not matching colors, decides where it goes.

GOAL: Place two rings and five cards into the red and blue panels so the reference sequence matches. CONTROLS: Click a tray item then a panel slot to place it. Space to submit. RULE: The two rings mark which red slots correspond to the blue panel's start. Red slots 2 and 3 held rings, leaving red 1, 4, and 5 for the remaining cards. TRAP: Assuming the blue panel reads right-to-left or the rings mark different slots caused failed alignment checks.

GOAL: Move the two yellow markers to the two marked cells in rows 3 and 6. CONTROLS: Red arrows shifted contents right or down; green arrows shifted contents left or up. RULE: Each click rotated a full row or column, moving markers one step in the chosen direction. TRAP: Believing markers needed to stay in the same row; they must travel along different lines to reach their separate targets.

GOAL: Cover every gray marker with the three movable shapes before the timer ran out. CONTROLS: Arrows shifted the active shape three cells; SPACE cycled which shape was active. RULE: A marker was satisfied only when a shape's body occupied its exact cell, not merely touched it. TRAP: I assumed the bar kept its full length when clipped against the wall; it actually shrank, so my first alignment fell short of the right marker.

GOAL: Make all marked cells orange, using four glyph stamps as the target pattern. CONTROLS: Click a cell to toggle its color; glyphs are read-only reference stamps. RULE: Each glyph is a colored stamp: it paints its white cells with its center ink color. Orange-center glyphs turn white cells orange; red-center glyphs leave them red. TRAP: Assuming all white cells in any glyph become orange regardless of center color, which over-painted the red-center regions.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking a green cross places a marker at a cell along its row. Clicking the marker merges crosses between the selected cross and the marker cell, leaving gray remnants. FAILED: Merging five crosses into four did not clear the level. Clicking gray crosses is a no-op. Pressing the key resets the board, losing merge progress. GOAL IS NOT: Reducing the cross count from five to four in a single sequence. CONTROLS: Clicking a green cross selects it and shows a marker. Clicking the marker performs the merge. Clicking the key resets the level.

GOAL: Fill the 5x4 grid so each cell matches its glyph: white means the center color, gray means the neighbor of center in the legend list. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell cycles its color forward through the legend order blue, red, orange. RULE: Gray maps to the legend neighbor of the center, not simply "not base and not center". TRAP: Assuming gray means the third color directly; for some centers this is ambiguous or wrong.

GOAL: Move the yellow token to the yellow-marked cell and the orange token to the orange-marked cell. CONTROLS: Red buttons rotated tokens along their respective loops; green buttons rotated them the opposite way. RULE: Each token followed only its own loop, except at the two shared cells where either loop could move it. TRAP: Assuming loops were separate; they actually intersected, allowing cross-loop movement at shared cells.

ESTABLISHED: The blue marker navigates a fixed maze; the red bar shifts position based on the blue's location, and a gray marker can be spawned via SPACE. FAILED: Reaching the bottom-right bracket with the blue marker is impossible in the current maze configuration. GOAL IS NOT: Simply navigating the blue marker to the bottom-right corner. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the blue marker. SPACE spawns or resets the gray marker and alters HUD state.

GOAL: align the plug's prong tips onto the green tabs and the bar into the socket. CONTROLS: arrows move the plug; SPACE rotates it. RULE: the bar must fill the hole exactly while tips cover the tabs. TRAP: assuming prongs could pass through walls; they must stay clear.

GOAL: Move yellow to the bottom-right cross center and orange to the far right of that row. CONTROLS: Red arrows rotated the horizontal and vertical cycles one way; green arrows rotated them the opposite way. RULE: The horizontal and vertical cycles shared four intersection cells, allowing pieces to switch tracks at these junctions. TRAP: Assuming pieces stayed in their original loops; ignoring the shared cells prevented routing the yellow piece into the correct horizontal position.

GOAL: Land the mirrored gray copy exactly on the yellow target. CONTROLS: Down moves both pieces down; Left moves the gray copy right and the black piece left. RULE: The gray piece mirrors the black piece across the divider, so horizontal inputs are reversed. TRAP: Pressing Right moves the gray copy left, away from the target, wasting time.

ESTABLISHED: The left panel holds a 14x14 L-shape with a small red piece. The right panel displays two inverted T symbols (⊥) separated by a dashed line. The left panel's silhouette in all four rotation states does not match the right panel's target. FAILED: Rotating the L-shape to all four orientations (0, 90, 180, 270 degrees) did not trigger a match or clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching the L-shape's silhouette to the inverted T shapes on the right. CONTROLS: Rotation buttons cycle the L-shape's orientation. The dashed line and right panel symbols appear static and unresponsive t

GOAL: Place two yellow tokens on the two empty red cells in the top row. CONTROLS: Middle red and green arrows shift tokens along the long L-shaped path; top red and green arrows shift tokens along the short top-row loop. RULE: Each arrow moves every token one step in its designated direction, so all tokens move simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming the top row was a simple line; it is a closed loop where the leftmost and rightmost cells connect, allowing wrap-around moves.

GOAL: Match the target pattern, white on top and purple on the bottom, using a movable frame that paints half-planes. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the frame around the grid; SPACE paints the selected color; clicking swatches changes the paint color. RULE: Each frame position paints a fixed half-plane: flat-above paints the top half, lower-right paints the bottom half. TRAP: Assuming the frame paints the half nearest to it. The lower-right frame actually painted the bottom half, not the right half.

GOAL: Fill the board with four colored bands: purple upper-left, white lower-left, orange lower-right, orange upper-right. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the paint frame around the board; clicks select colors; space applies the current frame's stroke. RULE: Each frame position paints a distinct half-plane; the intersection of two strokes defines a region. TRAP: Believing the UP arrow from the up-right diagonal reaches the flat-above position; it is a no-op, requiring LEFT instead.

ESTABLISHED: The sky contains 9 green blocks across 3 row bands; clicking each green block converts it to sky, widening its row's bar. FAILED: Opening all 9 green blocks did not clear the level; partial bars remained at rows 41-42 and 48-60. GOAL IS NOT: Simply opening every green block to maximize bar width. CONTROLS: LEFT/RIGHT moves the plug along the bottom; clicking a green block turns it into sky.

GOAL: Land the gray piece exactly on the yellow target, requiring you to first move the black piece away from the gray's path. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active piece; SPACE switched which piece was active; DOWN moved the black piece down. RULE: The divider always stays to the right of the black piece, forcing you to move the black piece down to clear the gray's path. TRAP: Thinking the black piece needed to land on the yellow target; the vertical-flip shape made exact overlap impossible, wasting actions on the wrong piece.

GOAL: Overlap both blocks onto the same black cell to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrows moved blocks simultaneously; if one target was a wall, that block stayed while the other moved. RULE: A move is valid if the destination is black; walls cause a safe halt, but checker patterns trigger a reset. TRAP: Assuming blocked moves onto checker strips were safe halts like wall blocks; they actually reset the level, costing extra actions.

GOAL: Paint the block to match the target, including a small orange rectangle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotated the main frame. Color swatches selected the paint. The SPACE bar painted a half-plane. Clicking the small frame's fill stamped a rectangle. RULE: Each orientation painted a different half-plane, building the pattern layer by layer. TRAP: Assuming the small frame's stamp location was fixed. It moved with the main frame, requiring repositioning to the correct orientation before stamping the orange rectangle.

GOAL: Place the black L and T onto the lower yellow shapes while their mirror images land on the upper yellows. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected piece or divider; space cycled which piece was active. RULE: The divider acts as a mirror; moving it down shifts all reflections upward, allowing simultaneous matches above and below. TRAP: Believing the pieces must stay above the divider; the solution required moving everything down to align reflections with the top targets.

GOAL: Build a four-color diagonal stripe pattern with a yellow stamp in the lower left. CONTROLS: Click swatches to pick colors; arrows move the brush frame; space applies the current color to the frame's region. RULE: Each brush paints a half-plane defined by a diagonal or vertical boundary, layering over previous colors. TRAP: Assuming the diagonal boundary was at sum 70 when it should have been 69, leaving extra purple cells.

GOAL: Match each marker's color by sliding objects over them. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected object; Space switched between the plus and X. RULE: An object changed color when it crossed a square of that hue, then matched markers of the same color. TRAP: The ball stays on the object you last moved, so switching with Space can leave you pushing the wrong piece.

ESTABLISHED: The W's tip at (12,5) coincides with the Y's tip; both red blocks sit at the same lattice point. The yellow's mouth accepts the W's tip. FAILED: Moving the W alone to connect with the Y did not clear the level. The p's other tip gets hidden under the W's body when the W is at (8,4). GOAL IS NOT: Simply connecting the W and Y tips. CONTROLS: DOWN/LEFT move the active object in lattice steps. Clicking an object selects it.

ESTABLISHED: The orange line holds three gray leaves at (6,25), (9,49), and (21,8); the purple line holds two at (28,60) and (54,46); the white token sits on the orange leaf at (6,25). FAILED: Clicking (27,60) did not move the white to an empty cell; instead it swapped the white with the purple leaf at (28,60), proving that clicks inside any leaf's diamond trigger a swap. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching a specific coordinate with the white token, since the white's position is determined by which leaf it occupies. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell inside a leaf's diamond swaps the white with that leaf; clicking

GOAL: Fill a diamond shape with red, blue, and orange bands. CONTROLS: Click palette colors to set the active ink; drag the frame to rotate its orientation. RULE: The frame stamps a solid rectangle of the active color at its current position and angle. TRAP: Assuming the red band was already placed; it remained blue until the red color was explicitly selected and stamped.

GOAL: Move the orange hub to its ring while keeping the purple hub valid. CONTROLS: Clicking a free cell moved the white; clicking a colored leaf's cell swapped the white with that leaf. RULE: A click is a swap if it lands in any leaf's diamond cell set, not just the leaf center. TRAP: Assuming clicks only move or swap at exact centers. Off-center clicks on leaf diamonds caused unexpected swaps, derailing the plan.

GOAL: Cover both crosses to win. CONTROLS: Space cycled active object. Arrows moved it. RULE: Reflections mirror across divider; divider moved with arrows. TRAP: Believed divider unselectable; it was, enabling win.

ESTABLISHED: Player stays in leftmost column; gates open at specific tank levels but return home after click. FAILED: Clicking orange gate B to align with door row; moving player to other columns; assuming win requires player Y at door row. GOAL IS NOT: Player reaching door row in current column; gate permanently sliding up on click. CONTROLS: Clicking gates slides them temporarily; clicking tanks adjusts levels; player moves within column.

GOAL: Reach the green exit while capturing all three red enemies. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player two lattice steps in that direction. RULE: Landing on a red enemy captures it, but entering the cell directly in front of a red enemy's facing direction triggers an instant capture of the player. TRAP: Assuming background cells are impassable; they are actually empty space that allows movement, though the black bar remains a solid wall.

GOAL: Move the plug's notch to the pink plus's column in the top bar. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows shifted the plug's notch along the bar. RULE: The nub always points in the direction of the last move. TRAP: Believing the nub must point left to face the pink; it only needed to be in the same column.

ESTABLISHED: The reading order is [B1,B2,B3, G1,G2,G3, red3]. The flash highlights the ring's red slot and the position-4 slot. The game wants Y at G1. FAILED: Clicking the yellow at G2 with the ring at red2, red3, or red1 did nothing. Moving the ring head changes the red slot but not the content's position. GOAL IS NOT: Placing Y at G2 or any position other than G1. CONTROLS: Clicking a red slot moves the ring head there. The content stays at G1. Clicking the yellow cell is a no-op.

GOAL: Guide the bright green hub to the marked target by clicking leaves to move it. CONTROLS: Click a leaf to merge it with the hub; the hub shifts toward the leaf's average position. RULE: The hub lands at the floor of the mean coordinate of all merged leaves. TRAP: Trusting the reported hub coordinate was costly; when the hub merged with other colors, the display showed the combined component's center, not the true hub position.

GOAL: Get all three yellow tokens onto the marked cells. CONTROLS: Click an arrow to rotate tokens along its associated line; clicking an arrow on an empty line did nothing. RULE: Each arrow defines a fixed cycle of cells; tokens move one step along that cycle per click. TRAP: Assuming arrow effects were independent of state; an arrow that seemed to swap cells on one line actually moved tokens on a completely different line, making earlier "no-op" observations misleading.

ESTABLISHED: The grid is a single piece moving one cell per press. Direction matters: pressing the same direction twice in a row is a no-op, except at specific cells where it triggers a teleport. FAILED: Repeated UP moves from (6,4) did nothing. Pressing DOWN from (1,8) after arriving via DOWN teleported the piece to (7,4) instead of moving to (2,8). GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the bottom-right corner (9,9) or (9,8). The target is likely (9,6) or requires a specific path through column 8. CONTROLS: UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT move one cell. Consecutive same-direction presses are blocked unless they

ESTABLISHED: Clicking swaps bar positions and widths. Blue bar moves right with arrows. Red bars reappear in vacated cells. Ball sits at bottom right. FAILED: Clicking red at rows 16-19 cols 8-19 then pressing SPACE did not clear. Clicking that red then the other red then SPACE also failed. Clicking center of red bar did not trigger win. GOAL IS NOT: Simply swapping blue with red bars once or twice. Blue does not need to reach ball position directly. CONTROLS: Click swaps blue with clicked bar. Arrows move blue bar. SPACE attempts to clear level.

GOAL: Align the black shape's mirrored copies with the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active object; Space cycled control between the vertical divider, black shape, and horizontal divider. RULE: The black shape reflects across both dividers; the yellow target is the union of these reflections. TRAP: Believing the yellow target was the black shape's direct position rather than its reflections.

GOAL: Deliver the plus to the blue target while it carries the blue marker. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plus; SPACE cycles to the next object. RULE: The plus changes color when its bar overlaps a marker's block, matching the marker's color. TRAP: Assuming the plus's current row was sufficient to hit the blue block, ignoring that the bar's horizontal span missed the block's columns.

ESTABLISHED: The maze is a spiral. Blocks are confined to the left pocket; the yellow marker is confined to the right pocket. They are separated by blocked gaps and cannot reach each other or the top corridors. FAILED: Clicking black cells or markers to recolor blocks or move them. Attempts to move blocks or the yellow across blocked gaps. GOAL IS NOT: Simply matching colors or having blocks and yellow occupy the same cell, as they are physically separated. CONTROLS: Clicking black cells turns blocks sky blue. Clicking a marker turns blocks gray and that marker yellow.

GOAL: Get the white marker to the marked cell by swapping it with gray leaves along three lines. CONTROLS: Click a leaf on the line the white occupies; the white and that gray swap positions. RULE: A line's hub is the midpoint of its two outer leaves; clicking a leaf moves the white to it. TRAP: Assuming all grays show as separate dots — one gray merged with the board's gray border, hiding a leaf and making a line look shorter.

ESTABLISHED: Four 6-tall mice on a 20-col grid. M3 pushed M4 right flush against the purple wall. M3 pushed M2 up. M2 pushed M1 right. All pushes worked when the target's leading edge was occupied. FAILED: Nothing failed yet; all pushes succeeded. GOAL IS NOT: Unknown. Not yet achieved. CONTROLS: Mouse click selects a piece. LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN move 3 cells. Pushes slide the adjacent piece until it hits a wall or another piece.

GOAL: Guide the token to the rightmost cell by following the yellow markers. CONTROLS: Click left/right arrows to move the token one cell in that direction. RULE: The yellow markers indicate the target cell; move the token toward them until it lands there. TRAP: Assuming markers always flank the target cell directly; they can appear offset or on adjacent cells, requiring careful observation of their exact position relative to the lattice.

GOAL: Clear the board by merging all crosses in a single row into one cell. CONTROLS: Click a cross to select it; click the adjacent empty cell in the same row to move it there, absorbing any cross it passes. RULE: A cross moves to an adjacent empty cell, capturing the cross between them. TRAP: Clicking coordinates based on visual position rather than logical row indices caused clicks to land in the wrong row, resulting in no-ops instead of merges.

GOAL: Slide four mice into matching holes on four separate frames. CONTROLS: Click a mouse to select it, then use arrow buttons to move it one cell per press.
